narrative.title: Investment thesis
narrative.inputsTitle: I. Data scope and synthesis method
narrative.inputsBody: The model evaluates five classes of variables: (1) quarterly financial statements and earnings quality; (2) capital structure, leverage, and operating cash flow; (3) technical market signals and price-volume state; (4) macro conditions, policy, interest rates, and credit; and (5) real-estate-specific attributes, news flow, and sentiment. In the current observation set, the most supportive group is {strongest} ({strongestScore}/100), while the most restrictive group is {weakest} ({weakestScore}/100).

decision.positive: With an AI score of {score}/100, expected upside of {upside}%, and confidence of {confidence}%, the BUY conclusion is supported by {strongest} as the main pillar ({strongestScore}/100), an average radar score of {radarAverage}/100, and a {spread}-point spread between the strongest and weakest groups. The constraint to monitor is {weakest} ({weakestScore}/100); with {warnings} warnings and {imputed} imputed features, the buy case remains preferable only if the weakest group does not deteriorate.
decision.neutral: With an AI score of {score}/100, expected upside of {upside}%, and confidence of {confidence}%, the HOLD conclusion reflects insufficient agreement across score groups. {strongest} is currently the strongest support ({strongestScore}/100), but {weakest} is only {weakestScore}/100, creating a {spread}-point gap versus the leading group. The average radar score is {radarAverage}/100; together with {warnings} warnings and {imputed} imputed features, this favors observation over adding exposure.
decision.negative: With an AI score of {score}/100, expected upside of {upside}%, and confidence of {confidence}%, the SELL conclusion follows from a weaker reward/risk profile and an average radar score of {radarAverage}/100. Although {strongest} remains the relative support ({strongestScore}/100), {weakest} at {weakestScore}/100 lowers the overall profile; the {spread}-point dispersion, {warnings} warnings, and {imputed} imputed features make risk reduction the preferred stance.

narrative.flowTitle: IV. Implications for money flow and market psychology

flow.positive: {recommendation} implies a more constructive psychological regime for quantitative and trend-following investors. Nevertheless, incremental inflow still depends on confirming liquidity, credit conditions, and the broader market backdrop. Current risk warnings: {warnings}.
flow.neutral: {recommendation} reflects an equilibrium between opportunity and risk. Capital flows are likely to await additional confirmation from the next quarterly financial statements, real-estate credit, policy execution, and price action. Market psychology therefore remains cautious, favoring observation over aggressive accumulation. Current risk warnings: {warnings}.
flow.negative: {recommendation} implies a more defensive psychological regime. Short-term capital may reduce exposure or rotate toward lower-risk tickers; re-entry depends on clear improvement in macro, credit, legal, liquidity, or earnings conditions. Current risk warnings: {warnings}.
